quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it is moving slowly. You may see this sign on farm equipment, farm vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It is a solid orange triangle during the day and appears as a hollow red triangle at night.

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if other vehicles are blocking your way, even if your light is green. If the light changes to red while you are in the intersection, you will block other traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: What word appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagon (eight-sided) sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back to the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only move back to the driving lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the driving lane.

questions.question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not assume the other driver will make space for you.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the other driver will make space for you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even when you signal.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what is the best way to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for on-ramps ahead on an interstate. When it is safe, move to the left lane to allow vehicles to enter from the on-ramps on your right.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one in front when it is hard to see at night. Use your headlights and follow the rules for high beams and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights to avoid being blinded by the glare.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams will reflect off these weather conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening around you. Watch the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle to see problems early. This will help you change your speed or position before danger occurs.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with stop signs on all four corners at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the other traffic on the road, as long as they are driving within the speed limit. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Most crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or road edge.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass, but only if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left, they:

options.text: May use the left lane.
May cut through all lanes.
May wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: May use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see bicyclists in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and see an emergency vehicle with its siren and flashing lights approaching. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right and stop before leaving the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: It is dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely because:

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as cars.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
They brake slower than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the motorcyclist at risk. You need enough space to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist makes a sudden stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for dangers. This sign tells you to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your instrument panel lights bright so other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Always drive slow enough to stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your vehicle and a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle stops suddenly or the rider falls. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often causes risky driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often causes risky driving choices.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky driving choices.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn in that direction after slowing down and checking traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
May turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: How often should you check your speedometer?

options.text: Once every ten minutes
Twice a minute
Once a minute

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a minute
questions.explanation: Check your speedometer about once every minute to make sure you are driving at a safe and legal speed. Make this a habit.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill curve. You should:

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: Your vehicle wheels went off the edge of the road. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge your car back onto the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Once your speed drops, check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel back onto the road. This can cause you to lose control or cross into other lanes.

questions.question: When dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped when a school bus flashes red lights with its stop arm out. You can proceed only after the lights turn off, the stop arm goes up, and the bus moves.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain starts, you should:

options.text: Avoid sharp turns and hard stops while driving fast.
Test your tire grip while driving uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sharp turns and hard stops while driving fast.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slowly to avoid skidding. Do not make fast turns or sudden stops on slippery roads.

questions.question: What describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: Other drivers will do the right thing.
They expect mistakes from others and are ready to react.
They expect no favors and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They expect mistakes from others and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers watch for mistakes other drivers might make. They prepare to react and protect themselves.

questions.question: Drivers entering a highway from an acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway, yield to traffic already on it. Merge safely when there is space.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection when you arrive at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Vehicles then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Yield to all pedestrians crossing the street, whether in marked crosswalks or not. Always prioritize pedestrian safety.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is ahead.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school is nearby. Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can cause danger. Impatient drivers may take risky actions to pass you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when clear.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely and wait while the light stays red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when clear.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red signal like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.
